## Summary

The "Eyes", part 1: a deterministic DOM walker that finds every **visible, interactive** form control on a page — including those inside open Shadow DOM — tags each with a stable `data-vfe-id`, and assigns a human-facing `badgeIndex`.

Output is an ordered list of `DiscoveredElement` records consumed by A-2 (label/context) and A-3 (serialisation), and the DOM attributes consumed by E-2 (badges) and B-1/B-2 (action resolution).

## Why it's hard

Real pages contain: honeypot inputs explicitly positioned off-screen, hidden modal templates, `display: contents` wrappers, `opacity: 0` inputs that a CSS library re-shows on focus, `<button>`s rendered as 0×0, custom components with open shadow roots, and controls that exist only after hydration. A naive `querySelectorAll('input')` fails on all of these.

## Public API

```ts
// packages/dom-engine/src/eyes/discover.ts
export interface DiscoveredElement {
  vfeId: string;              // 'vfe_12'
  badgeIndex: number;         // 1..N, document order
  element: HTMLElement;
  tag: string;                // lowercase tag name
  htmlType: string | null;    // input type, or role
}

export interface DiscoveryOptions {
  root?: Document | ShadowRoot;
  maxElements?: number;       // default 250
  includeButtons?: boolean;   // default true
  debug?: boolean;            // collects exclusion reasons
}

export interface DiscoveryResult {
  elements: DiscoveredElement[];
  excluded: Array<{ vfeId?: string; tag: string; reason: VisibilityReason }>;
  durationMs: number;
}

export function discoverInteractiveElements(
  options?: DiscoveryOptions,
): DiscoveryResult;

export function isVisible(el: Element): { visible: boolean; reason?: VisibilityReason };

export type VisibilityReason =
  | 'display-none' | 'visibility-hidden' | 'opacity-0' | 'zero-size'
  | 'aria-hidden' | 'inert' | 'offscreen-honeypot' | 'content-visibility-hidden'
  | 'type-hidden' | 'detached' | 'max-elements';

export function findByVfeId(
  id: string,
  root?: Document | ShadowRoot,
): HTMLElement | null;

export function clearVfeTags(root?: Document | ShadowRoot): void;
```

`findByVfeId` must search the document **and every open shadow root** (recursive `querySelectorAll` does not pierce shadow boundaries) — B-1/B-2 depend on this.

## Technical specification

### 1. Candidate selectors

```ts
const SELECTORS = [
  'input:not([type="hidden"])',
  'textarea',
  'select',
  'button',
  '[role="button"]',
  '[role="checkbox"]',
  '[role="combobox"]',
  '[role="listbox"]',
  '[role="radio"]',
  '[role="switch"]',
  '[role="textbox"]',
  '[role="spinbutton"]',
  '[role="option"]',        // only inside a role=listbox (see rule 4)
  '[contenteditable="true"]',
  'a[href]',                // optional: only when data-vfe-link or inside a form (config flag)
].join(',');
```

Exclusions applied **before** visibility work (cheap first):
- `input[type=hidden]`, `input[type=file]` (out of MVP scope — document as limitation), `input[type=submit|reset]`, `input[type=image]` — these are represented by their `<button>`/`[role=button]` siblings or not actionable by voice.
- `[disabled]` / `aria-disabled="true"` elements are still **discovered** (they are visible context and the Brain needs to know they exist) but flagged `disabled: true` in A-3. Do not drop them.
- Elements already tagged `[data-vfe-ignore]` (escape hatch for site owners).

### 2. Shadow DOM piercing

Use a manual worklist, not `TreeWalker` alone:

```ts
const found: Element[] = [];
const queue: Array<Document | ShadowRoot | Element> = [root];

while (queue.length) {
  const node = queue.shift()!;
  // 1. query candidates in this root
  const candidates = Array.from(node.querySelectorAll(SELECTORS));
  // 2. enqueue every shadow host found in this root
  for (const el of node.querySelectorAll('*')) {
    if (el.shadowRoot?.mode === 'open') queue.push(el.shadowRoot);
    else if (el.shadowRoot) { /* closed: unreachable, record debug note */ }
  }
  found.push(...candidates);
}
```

Requirements:
- Only **open** shadow roots are traversable. Closed roots (`attachShadow({mode:'closed'})`) are a documented, unavoidable limitation — record them under `excluded` with reason `detached`? No: add a `debug` note `closed-shadow-root` (not a `VisibilityReason`); do not crash.
- Same-origin iframes: **out of scope for A-1** (see "Non-goals"); cross-origin are impossible without `all_frames` + per-frame injection.
- Deduplicate by `Element` identity (a node can match multiple selectors) using a `Set<Element>`.
- Detached nodes (`!el.isConnected`) are excluded (`detached`).

### 3. Visibility algorithm (authoritative order)

```ts
function isVisible(el: Element): { visible: boolean; reason?: VisibilityReason } {
  if (!el.isConnected) return { visible: false, reason: 'detached' };

  // 3.1 aria-hidden + inert on self or any ancestor (walk up to root, crossing shadow boundaries via host)
  for (let n: Element | null = el; n; n = parentOf(n)) {
    if (n.getAttribute?.('aria-hidden') === 'true') return { visible: false, reason: 'aria-hidden' };
    if ((n as HTMLElement).inert === true) return { visible: false, reason: 'inert' };
  }

  // 3.2 computed style on self (single getComputedStyle per element, cached per pass)
  const cs = getComputedStyle(el);
  if (cs.display === 'none') return { visible: false, reason: 'display-none' };
  if (cs.visibility === 'hidden' || cs.visibility === 'collapse')
    return { visible: false, reason: 'visibility-hidden' };
  if (cs.contentVisibility === 'hidden') return { visible: false, reason: 'content-visibility-hidden' };

  // 3.3 opacity: 0 on self OR any ancestor (opacity is inherited visually, not by CSS cascade)
  for (let n: Element | null = el; n; n = parentOf(n)) {
    if (parseFloat(getComputedStyle(n).opacity) === 0)
      return { visible: false, reason: 'opacity-0' };
  }

  // 3.4 zero-size / no box
  const rects = el.getClientRects();
  const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
  if (rects.length === 0 || r.width === 0 || r.height === 0)
    return { visible: false, reason: 'zero-size' };

  // 3.5 honeypot / off-screen positioning
  //     absolute/fixed, positioned far outside the viewport, or clipped to 1x1
  if (r.right < -500 || r.bottom < -500 || r.left > innerWidth + 5000 || r.top > innerHeight + 5000)
    return { visible: false, reason: 'offscreen-honeypot' };
  if (r.width <= 1 && r.height <= 1) return { visible: false, reason: 'zero-size' };

  return { visible: true };
}
```

Rules and rationale:
- **Do not** exclude elements merely because they are below the fold. Scrolling is cheap; losing fields is not.
- `display: contents` on an ancestor yields a zero-size rect for the ancestor but the child still has a box — evaluate rects **on the element only**, never on ancestors.
- `opacity: 0` inputs re-shown on focus: excluded is correct per spec, **but** custom checkboxes often hide the native input exactly this way. Mitigation: if the element is an `input[type=checkbox|radio]` and it has an associated visible `<label>`/`aria-labelledby`, treat it as visible and mark `viaProxy: true` in the debug record (A-2 will resolve the label; B-2 will click the proxy). Same for `select` styled with `appearance:none`.
- `parentOf(n)`: `n.parentElement ?? (n.getRootNode() as ShadowRoot).host ?? null` — this is what makes ancestor checks pierce shadow boundaries.
- Cache `getComputedStyle` results in a `Map<Element, CSSStyleDeclaration>` **per discovery pass**; never call `getBoundingClientRect` interleaved with style *writes* (only reads here).
- `:disabled` is not a visibility signal.

### 4. Special cases

| Case | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `[role="option"]` | Include only when an ancestor `[role="listbox"]` is visible — i.e. an **open** custom dropdown. Otherwise skip (option spam). |
| Radios | Each `<input type=radio>` is a separate element (action target must be unambiguous). A-2 attaches the group legend as `groupLabel`. |
| `<select>` | One element; its `<option>`s are serialised by A-3 as `options`. |
| Buttons | Include `<button>`, `input[type=button]`, `[role=button]`; dedupe when a `<button>` has `role=button` (single node anyway). |
| `contenteditable` | Include `[contenteditable="true"]` and `[contenteditable=""]`; `contenteditable="false"` is excluded. |
| Hidden native checkbox behind CSS | Keep, `viaProxy` debug flag (see above). |
| `<fieldset disabled>` | Children remain visible but A-3 must report `disabled: true`. |
| Repeater rows (React tables) | No special handling; document order defines badges. |

### 5. ID tagging & stability

- `data-vfe-id="vfe_<n>"` — the counter is **monotonic per page load**, never reused.
- Stability across re-scans: keep `WeakMap<Element, string>` module-scoped. If an element already has an ID, reuse it. This is what lets B-1 fill `vfe_7` after the page re-rendered around it (same node) and lets the Brain refer to `badgeIndex` consistently while an input keeps focus.
- `badgeIndex` is **recomputed each pass** in document order (`1..N`) — it is a *presentation* number, not an identity. The Brain must always emit `targetId` (`vfe_*`), never a raw badge number; C-1 converts "field 4" to `vfe_*` server-side.
- Tag writes are guarded: if `el.getAttribute('data-vfe-id') === id`, do not write (avoids MutationObserver feedback).
- Tag the DOM **after** the full discovery pass completes (single write phase) to avoid layout thrash and mutation storms.
- `clearVfeTags()` removes `data-vfe-*` attributes everywhere (called on HUD teardown and by the testbed reset).

### 6. Ordering

Document order, **not** visual order, with one exception: fixed-position dialogs (`[role=dialog]`, `aria-modal=true`) discovered later in the DOM are **hoisted to the front** of the list so the Brain sees the active modal first and E-2 numbers it 1..k. Implementation: stable partition `modalElements` + `rest`, preserving document order inside each group.

### 7. Performance budget

- 300 visible controls on a mid-tier laptop: **≤ 40 ms** for the full pass (measured with `performance.now()` in a Playwright benchmark on the testbed "stress" route with 500 inputs).
- No forced synchronous layout in a loop: batch all reads before any writes.
- `maxElements` (default 250) hard cap; when hit, stop walking and add `{ reason: 'max-elements' }` to `excluded`. Prevents pathological pages from freezing the tab and from blowing up the LLM prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a fixture containing hidden honeypots, a hidden modal, and visible inputs, only visible interactable elements are returned.
- [ ] Every returned element has a unique `data-vfe-id="vfe_N"` and a sequential `badgeIndex` starting at 1.
- [ ] Open shadow DOM roots are pierced; closed roots do not throw.
- [ ] Re-running discovery reuses the same `data-vfe-id` for the same DOM node and does not duplicate attributes.
- [ ] Hidden native checkbox/radio behind a visible label is still discoverable (`viaProxy`).
- [ ] Modal controls are ordered before background controls.
- [ ] 500-element stress page discovers in ≤ 40 ms locally (CI allowance ×3).
- [ ] No `console.*` output in production build; `debug: true` returns exclusion reasons without logging.
- [ ] `clearVfeTags()` leaves zero `data-vfe-*` attributes in the document and all shadow roots.
- [ ] Unit tests cover every `VisibilityReason` branch (coverage ≥ 95% on `discover.ts` / `visibility.ts`).

## Non-goals / documented limitations

- Closed shadow roots, cross-origin iframes, and same-origin iframes (candidate for a follow-up ticket `A-4`, not MVP).
- `input[type=file]` uploads (no voice story; excluded).
- Canvas/WebGL-rendered forms (no DOM, unsolvable generically).
- Multi-select `<select multiple>` (serialised but `SELECT` only sets one value — see B-2).
